source: Five user photographs of the Passaporte para Português glossary: pages 136, 138, 140, 142 and 144, including readable following-page fragments
normalization_notes: Manually transcribe pages 136, 138, 140, 142 and 144 and readable following-page fragments. Page 136 is identified from its position between previously imported pages 135 and 137; its printed number is obscured.
Exclude running publisher text, headings and page numbers. Printed references identify book sections, not CEFR levels.
Use lowercase NFC individual words; remove punctuation and trailing gender articles. Retain articles/prepositions within expressions.
Expand Exmos. as excelentíssimos, with dictionary verification. Do not insert the punctuation-bearing abbreviation as a word.
Expand loiro/louro, loiça/louça and meu/minha into separate word forms; o/a annotations on fã and fadista do not imply distinct spellings.
Split importar-se and mudar-se into base verb plus se. Retain original pronominal constructions for context.
Expand faz/por favor into faz, por and favor. Keep the lexical compound mal-educado intact.
Translate each component independently. Keep complete source expressions and the photographed German meanings in rows.
Repeated meanings such as metro (transport/measurement), ligar and mulher share one normalized word while their source occurrences remain distinct.
Deduplicate overlaps with earlier batches. Do not infer cropped rows below the page edge.

dictionary_checks.note: Verified Exmo. expands to Excelentíssimo; source plural expanded to excelentíssimos.
Verified the Portuguese draught-beer noun, matching the German gloss.
Verified European Portuguese acute-accent spelling and noun meanings.
Both extraction-site and explosive-device senses are valid; both are explicitly distinguished in the translations.

translation_notes: Expansion of Exmos. is recorded alongside the printed abbreviation. Excelentíssimos is formal address and is estimated B2 rather than automatically labeled beginner vocabulary.
Fã and fadista have the same spelling for either gender; senhores is the separate plural form.
Facto is fact; fato is the existing European Portuguese clothing word suit. Neither is substituted for the other.
Falta is the noun absence/lack; the meaning to miss belongs to the complete sentir a falta de expression retained in JSON.
Gente means people; a gente can mean we as an expression. The full expression is not assigned to every component.
Gabinete and prova are translated independently; the entire fitting-room meaning belongs to gabinete de prova.
Importar-se de is a polite would-you-mind construction. The standalone verb includes matter/import and mind with se, not the full polite request.
Imperial is translated as draught beer from the photographed noun, not the unrelated adjective imperial.
Livre means free/available/unoccupied, while the existing gratuito is free of charge.
Loiro/louro and loiça/louça are retained as distinct source spelling alternatives and deduplicated individually.
Grama is already stored as the mass unit gram. Metro as metre is a contextual gap retained in JSON because the existing record means subway.
Mina retains two dictionary-verified meanings in translations without claiming the short German gloss uniquely selects one.
Existing ficar, mulher and mesmo already cover the photographed meanings and are preserved.
New entries start at mastery 0. Existing IDs, translations, levels and practice history are preserved.
